title: Polarity node — the one home (s238-D1)
description: A polarity is a permanent pull between two (or more) true things that is managed, never solved (s238-D4). It is a hyper-relational NODE with N typed parties and typed out-links to rulings; pairwise edges are DERIVED for consumers, never authored (s238-D1). This schema carries NO status field (s238-D3 / s237-D9: settled-by-obligation / resolved / open is derived at build time with a clock) and NO free-text judgement field of any name (s238-D7 refusal 3): the node's only judgement is a typed link to a knowledge/_rulings.json id. `additionalProperties: false` at every level is what makes refusals 3 and 5 structural rather than a list of banned words. Enforced by knowledge/_validate_polarities.py, which READS this file (the consumer's grammar) and never re-types its rules.

id.description: pl-NN. The rename tension -> polarity happened before generation (s238-D4); the former tn-NN id is kept under sources[].id, never as an alias here.

parties.description: The things being pulled. Every ref MUST resolve against the live registers: a principle or obligation row in knowledge/brain/principles.json, a ruling id in knowledge/_rulings.json, or a declared stub in knowledge/brain/stubs.json (s238-D1; refusal 1). A party's KIND (principle / obligation / ruling / stub) is DERIVED from where the ref resolves — an obligation is a register row whose grade is L (s237-D1, s237-D2) — and is never typed here. The same ref may not appear twice on one node; a node may not be its own party; another polarity may not be a party.

ref.description: ASCII id of a principle / obligation (pr-…), a ruling (as spelled in _rulings.json) or a stub (st-…).

role.description: Which side of the pull the party stands on. Parties on the SAME side pull together (lane T finding 4: tn-19's three persuasion principles are one side) and produce no derived edge between them.

note.description: A verbatim gloss carried from the source row (e.g. the parenthetical after a principle id). At most 15 words — a note is a receipt, not a place for a judgement (refusal 3).

mediating_variable.description: The variable that decides which party wins in a given case — the thing that is MANAGED. Descriptive, carried from the source row.

links.description: Typed out-links to rulings ONLY (s238-D6: 'RULING LINKS ON A POLARITY ARE TYPED … the generator refuses an untyped one'). The four types and what each asserts, with the subject named because two of them are worded from the ruling's side: resolvedBy — the POLARITY is settled in this house by the ruling (its route is the ruling; lane T's R-RESOLVED); explainedBy — the RULING is explained by this polarity's principles (the s237-D5 relation: one-directional and advisory; a principle may explain a ruling and can never overturn one); challengedBy — the RULING is challenged by this polarity (advisory; the ruling stands until Dave rules; lane T finding 2 names tn-11 and tn-14); touches — the polarity and the ruling are adjacent and nothing stronger is claimed (the least claim; it never closes an open question). A fifth type is NOT ruled and is refused (refusal 2). A link to a principle, a stub or another polarity is refused (refusal 1): parties carry principles; edges are derived.

ref.description: A ruling id present in knowledge/_rulings.json and not superseded (a ruling carrying `superseded_by` is not live: point at its successor).

quote.description: The <=15-word verbatim quote that justifies the TYPE — a receipt, not a judgement (refusal 3).

sources.description: Where the row came from: the frozen register row that keeps the words this node does not carry (the_pull, how_it_resolves — ADR-0017: the node points, the source keeps the words).

path.description: Repo-relative path of the source register.

id.description: The row id inside that register (e.g. tn-01).

x-vocabulary: `maxWords` is a house keyword (a standard validator ignores it; knowledge/_validate_polarities.py enforces it). Everything else is draft 2020-12 core: type · required · additionalProperties · properties · items · enum · pattern · minItems · minLength.

x-refusals.description: The five refusals of s238-D7, named as the validator prints them. Listed here so the schema and the gate cannot describe two different contracts; the enforcement lives in knowledge/_validate_polarities.py.
x-refusals.R1: a party or link ref that does not resolve against the live registers (sub-forms: R1-DANGLING · R1-SUPERSEDED · R1-SELF-PARTY · R1-CIRCULAR · R1-WRONG-REGISTER · R1-UNDECLARED-STUB)
x-refusals.R3: a judgement text field of any name on a node (sub-forms: R3-JUDGEMENT-FIELD · R3-QUOTE-TOO-LONG · R3-NOTE-TOO-LONG)
x-refusals.R4: an authored edge file — pairwise edges exist only under _generated/ with a content-freshness check (sub-forms: R4-AUTHORED-GENERATED · R4-AUTHORED-EDGES · R4-STRAY-FILE)
x-refusals.R5: a typed status on a node (R5-TYPED-STATUS)
